For one faculty position we will consider candidates with interests and experience in other experimentally-oriented areas of research in particle astrophysics as well as interest in AMS. Research presently underway in the department includes several particle astrophysics experiments: (1) the Antarctic Impulsive Transient Antenna (ANITA) ultra-high energy (UHE) neutrino experiment, (2) the Airshower Microwave Bremsstrahlung Radiometer (AMBER) augmentation to the Auger Observatory for UHE cosmic rays, (3) the Askaryan Radio Array (ARA), a new UHE neutrino initiative at the South Pole; (4) the continuing long-term efforts in the Super-Kamiokande neutrino physics, astrophysics, and nucleon decay detector in Japan, (5) new initiatives in the DUSEL underground laboratory, and (6) a growing program in anti-electron neutrino studies aimed at reactor monitoring, geophysics, particle and astrophysics.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Position in Neutrino Physics
jobs.description:
The Caltech experimental high energy physics group is seeking highly qualified candidates for a postdoctoral research position in neutrino physics. Our group is centrally involved in the NOvA and MINOS long-baseline experiments, and we are engaged in the development of a new technique for kinematic neutrino mass measurements.

NOvA's unique detector design, off-axis location, and 810 km baseline permit a broad program of neutrino oscillation physics, including a sensitive search for muon-neutrino to electron-neutrino oscillations. The primary goals of NOvA are to measure the neutrino mixing angle theta_{13}, to determine the neutrino mass ordering, and to look for leptonic CP violation. NOvA will also make precision measurements of the dominant oscillation parameters using both neutrinos and antineutrinos, in search of field non-maximal, mixing and physics beyond the standard model. Our group has central roles in NOvA physics analysis as well as in data acquisition and electronics, detector commissioning and calibration; and event simulation and reconstruction. The NOvA near detector prototype is now operating at Fermilab, and the far detector is expected to turn on in 2012.

The MINOS experiment continues to produce leading neutrino oscillation results in the atmospheric sector, and the data we collect in the upcoming medium-energy NuMI run will allow for numerous novel searches for physics beyond the standard model, including non-standard interactions and sterile states.

Our group is also involved in the Project 8 experiment, which aims to develop a new radiofrequency electron detection technique for improved direct neutrino mass measurements using tritium beta decay. This effort includes a broad range of analysis and detector R&D toward defining the performance and scalability of the design.

It is expected that the successful candidate would play an important role in one or more of the above efforts. Candidates should have a Ph.D. in high energy physics and should demonstrate strong potential for outstanding achievement as an independent researcher. Experience with detector hardware and with object-oriented software and analysis design will be advantageous.

Interested applicants should send a cover letter, curriculum vitae, list of publications, and description of research interests and skills to Professor Ryan Patterson (email: rbpatter@caltech.edu), High Energy Physics, MC 356-48 Caltech, Pasadena, CA 91125. Applicants should also arrange for three letters of reference to be sent. Electronic submission of materials is preferred. The position is available immediately, and review of applications will continue until the position is filled.

Caltech is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. Women, minorities, veterans and disabled persons are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Software for ATLAS: C++, Python, Unix, Linux
jobs.description:
KEY SKILLS: Software developer, High Energy Physics, Parallel Computing, Performance Optimization, C++, Python, Unix, Linux

POSITION SUMMARY: As a member of the Physics Division, optimize high energy physics data analysis applications to run efficiently on multicore and manycore CPUs. Join a dynamic team of scientists and engineers in the Physics Division and in CRD Advanced Computing for Science department, to develop and to support athena, the common control framework for the ATLAS experiment at CERN that is about to start data taking. The athena framework supports event reconstruction and simulation, event filtering and physics analysis. Optimizing the performance of athena on multicore and manycore CPUs is expected to be a major component of this work. One promising avenue would be to use athena data flow information to partition athena event processing in sub tasks with minimal data dependencies. Another area of interest would be to to investigate optimization strategies for clusters of OOP function calls either by using standard C++ constructs like function inlining, or C++ compilers interprocedural optimization.

DUTIES: Required -- Design, develop, implement, and support object oriented scientific applications primarily implemented in the C++ programming language and tightly integrated with the Python scripting language. Interact with other project members and physicists and provide consultancy and support. Present work in journals and in seminars and conferences. Participate in group meetings and seminars. Travel to and reside at CERN in Geneva, Switzerland for at least short periods of time as required by the collaboration.

QUALIFICATIONS: Required -- University degree in Computer Science, High Energy Physics, Nuclear Science, or related field. Programming ability in C++ and Python. Significant experience using the Unix operating system, and in particular Linux. Ability to work in high-pressure environment and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing.

Desired -- Experience in development of HEP data analysis tools/applications in particular in the ATLAS environment. Hands-on knowledge of parallel programming techniques. Hands-on knowledge of GNU gcc optimization techniques and API Hands-on knowledge of Intel PTU analysis tools.

jobs.title: Experimental Neutrino and Nuclear Physics
jobs.description:
The Nuclear Science Division of the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory invites applications for a postdoctoral position in the neutrino and experimental low energy research program at the 88-Inch Cyclotron with a focus on the development of next generation gamma-ray detector arrays based on tracking technology. The successful candidate will be expected to participate in both the GRETINA/GRETA and low energy neutrino detector projects. The low energy neutrino project aims at using Ge detector for measuring neutrino and dark matter. GRETINA is a detector array based on highly-segmented Ge detectors with the ability to track gamma rays which promises to significantly increase the sensitivity in the detection of gamma radiation for nuclear physics applications.

The successful candidate will be involved in all development, construction, and research aspects of these projects, including perform simulation calculations of the detector properties, develop software for signal decomposition and tracking, and carry out measurements with the detector and analyze data. All these efforts are centered in the Nuclear Science Division with strong connection to the Engineering Division at LBNL as well as to complementary efforts at the University of California, Berkeley, particularly at the Department of Nuclear Engineering.

It is also expected that the candidate will contribute to the ongoing research programs at the 88-Inch Cyclotron, especially a program using the GRETINA array, and will be encouraged to initiate his/her own research. Current research areas include the study of exotic neutron-rich nuclei, proton-neutron correlations, and the structure of heavy nuclei.

Applicants are expected to hold a recent (within the last 2 years) Ph.D. in experimental nuclear science or related field. Experience in Ge gamma-ray detectors, associated electronics, and data acquisition hardware and software is desirable.

jobs.title: Scientific Computing
jobs.description:
KEY SKILLS DESIRED Scientific computing, physics background, applied mathematics, parallel programming

POSITION SUMMARY

The Scientific Computing Group has an immediate opening for a postdoctoral fellow to develop highly optimized parallel algorithms, codes and software tools for the analyses of X-ray scattering data collected at the Advanced Light Source (ALS). X-ray scattering is important in several energy critical applications pertinent to the Carbon Cycle 2.0 initiative at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.

DUTIES

The successful candidate will participate in research activities to develop novel high-performance algorithms and software tools for accelerating the computational speed of existing and new X-ray scattering analysis codes. The tasks include parallelization and performance optimization of existing and new codes at the ALS, as well as development of new physics required for accurate analysis of complex scattering data. The computational methods comprise 3D reverse Monte Carlo, molecular dynamics simulations, 3D FFT, and linear algebra algorithms. These codes need to be tuned on a number of medium-level to massively parallel computing platforms, including GPU clusters and large scale distributed-memory computers with multicore or hybrid node architectures such as Cray XT5 and Linux clusters.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required -- Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Physical Sciences, or Engineering within the last three years is required, with a strong background in scientific computing. Knowledge of mathematical physics is desirable, and a fundamental understanding of scattering is a plus. The candidate has to work in a highly creative and collaborative environment, should be able to program proficiently in a high-level language such as C, and should have experience in parallel computing. Excellent communication skills and being able to work independently are essential.

Notes

All positions require the completion of a background check. This is a one-year term appointment with the possibility of renewal. Salary for post-doctoral positions depends on years of experience post-degree.

jobs.description:

jobs.title: Information Technology Specialist
jobs.description:
As a member of the Astrophysics Data Systems (ADS) project, you will be part of a team working to design, develop, implement and maintain the project's IT infrastructure, and will help plan, specify, and build the technologies needed to support the project's goal of ubiquitous access to the astronomical literature and related datasets. As ADS is currently transitioning to an open-source digital library system, your initial primary focus will be the integration and customization of its two main components:

Invenio (for metadata management and curation) and SOLR (for indexing and searching).

The ideal candidate is a software developer with experience and knowledge of: Java, Python, SQL and Linux, database management systems, XML, XML transformation tools, and web standards, metadata standards and protocols in use in the Digital Library community, Information Retrieval and Information Extraction principles and practices.

The full description of this opening is available online at: http://www.cfa.harvard.edu/hr/postings/11-57.html and http://jobview.usajobs.gov/GetJob.aspx?JobID=101776971

About the ADS:
The SAO/NASA Astrophysics Data System (ADS) is a Digital Library portal for researchers in Astronomy and Physics, operated by the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory (SAO) under a NASA grant. The ADS maintains a bibliographic database of over 9 million records and a fulltext archive of over 1.5 million scholarly papers. More information about the ADS and its services is available at http://ads.harvard.edu and http://adslabs.org

The Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory is part of what is arguably the largest and most diverse astrophysical institution in the world, the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics (CfA). CfA staff carries out a broad program of research in astronomy, astrophysics, and earth and space sciences. More information about SAO and the CfA is available online at http://www.cfa.harvard.edu
